title: Demodulated Mirror-MoE expert views
hypothesis: For four context-addressed logical experts on a shared FFN, row-norm demodulation of learned Givens weight views improves mean fresh accuracy by at least 1.0pp and cuts context activation RMS coefficient of variation by at least 25% versus the identical undemodulated Mirror model, with <=1.1x payload bytes and <=1.2x active MACs versus IA3.
physical_object: one shared two-layer ReLU FFN classifier
mirror_coordinate: four context-specific Givens rotations on input planes, optionally followed by row-norm demodulation
controls: same Mirror Givens with row-norm demodulation

task.teacher: shared random two-layer ReLU classifier with four context Givens views and per-output row norm normalization

development.selection_metric: mean validation accuracy; ties resolved by lower cross entropy

success_gate: Fresh demodulated Mirror beats identical undemodulated Mirror by >=1.0pp accuracy and reduces context activation RMS coefficient of variation >=25%, and is not dominated by IA3/rank-one on quality, bytes, and active MACs.
failure_gate: Demodulation misses either preregistered Mirror-vs-Mirror condition or a simple control dominates quality at comparable or lower bytes/compute.
boundaries: Known context addresses; learned routing not tested.
Fixed-update performance is not a capacity claim.
